correctness.rationale: The positive/negative phase-pair conditional exponential tail is exact and continuous at the moving boundary; differentiating its normalized amplitude difference gives a strictly positive probability factor for every threshold below the larger crest. Direct endpoint signs yield exactly one reversal. The crossing identity reduces near the largest crest to a Bessel difference of order a^2 balanced against the arcsine edge integral of order d^(3/2)/sqrt(a), implying the explicit ratio-dependent 5/3 law. Parameters, edge cases and strict ranges are specified, and a deterministic standard-library checker independently evaluates finite examples. It is not a proof by numerical enumeration.

originality.rationale: Full accessible sources establish the underlying tide–surge convolution, skew-surge independence and approximation of sinusoidal tidal residence time, while no exact combination of all-amplitude ordering and the sharp ratio-dependent 5/3 near-crest coefficient was found in the actual inspections and targeted searches. The qualitative single crossing may follow from classical probability-order results; historical novelty is provisional with explicit residual risks.
residual_risks: A general stochastic-order or total-positivity theorem could imply the qualitative single-crossing law; it would not by itself supply the calculated sinusoidal 5/3 coefficient without additional work.
An obscure analytic treatment of exponential–arcsine convolutions could contain an equivalent asymptotic despite no identified direct match.

value.rationale: Coastal practitioners use tide/surge convolutions and simplified high/low-tide phase approximations. The exact sign of tidal-amplitude impacts changes once and is therefore not captured by a globally directioned approximation. The 5/3 exponent and explicit near-crest constant identify a natural singular geometric effect of slowing sinusoidal tide near its crest and give a sharp numerical benchmark with a distinct two-point approximation; a motivated quantitative fact rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
